items.q: A belief held with absolute conviction despite irrefutable contrary evidence, not culturally shared, is what?
items.exp: Delusions are defined by fixity, falsehood and cultural incongruence. Overvalued ideas are comprehensible and held less absolutely; obsessions are recognised as own and resisted; phobias are fears recognised as excessive.
r: Incorrect. Overvalued ideas allow some doubt and comprehensibility.
Correct. Fixed false culturally alien belief is delusion.
Incorrect. Obsessions are ego dystonic and resisted.
Incorrect. Phobia is recognised excessive fear.
items.kp: Unshakeable plus false plus alien equals delusion.

items.q: Patient insists his wife has been replaced by an identical impostor. This is which phenomenon?
items.exp: Capgras is delusional misidentification that a familiar person is replaced by an impostor. Fregoli is opposite (stranger is familiar in disguise); Cotard is nihilistic nonexistence; Ekbom is infestation delusion.
r: Incorrect. Fregoli believes strangers are familiar people disguised.
Correct. Impostor replacement is Capgras.
Incorrect. Cotard believes self or organs do not exist.
Incorrect. Ekbom is delusional parasitosis.

items.q: Voices heard as real in external space without any stimulus present are classified as what?
items.exp: True hallucinations lack stimulus yet carry full perceptual force in external objective space without insight. Pseudohallucinations are located in inner space with insight retained; illusions misread real stimuli.
r: Incorrect. Illusions need a real stimulus misinterpreted.
Correct. Stimulus free external perception is true hallucination.
Incorrect. Pseudohallucination keeps insight and inner location.
Incorrect. Afterimages are normal retinal phenomena.
items.kp: No stimulus, fully real, outside: true hallucination.

items.q: Predominantly visual hallucinations in an acutely unwell patient most strongly suggest what category?
items.exp: Visual hallucinations flag organic states: delirium, dementia with Lewy bodies, occipital lesions, drug intoxication or withdrawal. Auditory hallucinations dominate primary psychoses instead.
r: Incorrect. Schizophrenia hallucinates mainly in auditory modality.
Correct. Visual means organic until disproven.
Incorrect. Manic hallucinations are usually auditory and mood congruent.
Incorrect. Personality disorder does not produce true visual hallucinations.
items.kp: Seeing things means search the body and brain.

items.q: Thought broadcasting, insertion and withdrawal belong historically to which symptom group?
items.exp: Schneider listed passivity and thought alienation phenomena (insertion, withdrawal, broadcasting), third person voices and delusional perception as first rank for schizophrenia, though they occur in other psychoses too.
r: Incorrect. Bleuler emphasised association loosening, autism, ambivalence, affect.
Correct. First rank Schneider symptoms.
Incorrect. Negative symptoms are deficits like avolition.
Incorrect. Catatonia is motor syndrome.
items.kp: Thoughts inserted or broadcast: Schneider first rank.

items.q: Speech that answers questions only after excessive irrelevant detail, eventually reaching the point, shows what?
items.exp: Circumstantial speech over includes detail but reaches its goal; tangential speech never returns to the point. Word salad is incoherent; flight of ideas is rapid pressured topic shifting with links, typical of mania.
r: Incorrect. Tangentiality never reaches the answer.
Correct. Long way round but arrives: circumstantial.
Incorrect. Word salad lacks comprehensible links.
Incorrect. Flight is pressured and rapid with distractibility.

items.q: Feeling insects crawling under skin (formication) classically accompanies which state?
o: Cocaine intoxication and alcohol withdrawal states
items.exp: Tactile formication accompanies stimulant use (cocaine bugs) and delirium tremens spectrum states. It differs from Ekbom delusional infestation belief without true tactile perception context.
r: Correct. Stimulant and withdrawal states cause formication.
Incorrect. Depression hallucinates rarely and mood congruently.
Incorrect. Outdated term, not specific association.
Incorrect. OCD has intrusive thoughts, not formication.
items.kp: Crawling skin: think stimulants or withdrawal.

items.q: Which symptom group best predicts long term functional outcome in schizophrenia?
items.exp: Deficit (negative) symptoms correlate with poor social and occupational outcome and respond poorly to antipsychotics, whereas positive symptoms fluctuate and treat better. Rehabilitation targets negative burden.
r: Incorrect. Grandiosity fluctuates with episodes.
Correct. Negative symptoms predict disability.
Incorrect. Hallucinations treat relatively better.
Incorrect. Persecution theme does not grade outcome.
items.kp: It is the missing drive, not voices, that disables.

items.q: Hypnopompic hallucinations occur at what transition and signify what?
items.exp: Hypnopompic (on waking) and hypnagogic (on falling asleep) imagery are normal sleep border phenomena, also prominent in narcolepsy. They do not diagnose psychosis in isolation.
r: Incorrect. They occur at sleep wake borders.
Correct. On waking, normally benign.
Incorrect. Sleep onset is hypnagogic; neither alone means psychosis.
Incorrect. Seizure phenomena differ in stereotypy and consciousness.
items.kp: Half awake visions are usually normal.

items.q: A normal perception suddenly given delusional significance (a traffic light turning red means he is chosen) is termed what?
items.exp: Delusional perception (Schneider first rank) attaches abnormal self referential significance to an accurately perceived stimulus in one step. Secondary delusions instead elaborate understandably from prior psychopathology.
r: Incorrect. Secondary delusions derive from other symptoms understandably.
Correct. Instant delusional meaning on true perception.
Incorrect. Illusion misperceives the stimulus itself.
Incorrect. Overvalued ideas develop comprehensibly from personality.
items.kp: Seen correctly, meant delusionally: delusional perception.
